lines.text: A Royal Ward can't leave the city. But nobody had said I couldn't leave the palace. Holt said that if I went anywhere, he was coming. So did Ash. So did Oswin.
We went down into the Lowmarket. Mud to the ankle. Houses stacked on houses. And a smell that Ash found fascinating.
The Lowmarket children took one look at Ash and charged. Holt reached for his sword. Ash lay down in the mud and let them climb on him.
The line at the well was two hundred people long. The water that came up was brown.
You're the zero. The King's new pet. Come down to look at the poor, have you? Next time, bring a bucket.
Her name was Mags. She carried water for a living, two buckets on a yoke, up and down the Lowmarket from dawn to dark. A copper a bucket.
Why is there only one well?
Because the water used to come from up there.
She pointed at the aqueduct, marching across the sky on its tall stone legs. And at the gap in the middle, where one arch had fallen.
Twenty years ago, that arch came down. The lords up the hill dug their own wells. We got this one. The children get the coughing sickness every summer. Some of them don't get better.
The Crown's engineers looked at it once, my lord. They said it would cost too much. Nobody up the hill drinks from it, you see.
I climbed up to the broken arch, with Holt puffing behind me. I couldn't help it. I never can.
The channel above the gap was choked with twenty years of mud and weeds. But far up in the hills, I could hear it. Water. Still running. Still trying to come down.
It wasn't a ruin. It was a repair that nobody had bothered to make.
One arch fallen, eleven standing. Stone from the old quarry. A wooden frame to hold the curve. Fifty strong backs, and a month. Less, with the right fifty.
For the first time since the Stone, I wasn't thinking about the Stone.
What are you doing up there, zero?
Counting.
Counting what?
How many buckets you'll never have to carry again.
She laughed at me. Then she stopped laughing, and looked up at the arch, and didn't say anything at all.
On the way back down, Oswin stopped dead in the street. An old woman sat in a doorway, shelling beans. She was staring at him.
Sir Oswin Hale. Of the King's Third Company. I'd know that face among a thousand.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-one, coming soon.
